Question: Which Indian cricketer was the penultimate holder of the title Nawab of Pataudi?
Thought 1: I need to find out who held the title Nawab of Pataudi, and then identify the penultimate holder. I will start by searching for "Nawab of Pataudi".
Action 1: Search[Nawab of Pataudi]
Observation 1: Pataudi State was a small princely state in India, established in 1804 by the East India Company rule in India.. The state formed a part of the Delhi Territory in the Ceded and Conquered Provinces. It was under the suzerainty of the Commissioner of Delhi. It had an area of 52 square miles and included one town, Pataudi, and 40 villages, ruled by the Pataudi family.. The state of Pataudi was established in 1804 by the British East India Company, when Faiz Talab Khan, an Afghan Pashtun warlord of the Barech tribe, who was made the first Nawab, aided them in their battle against the Maratha Empire, during the Second Anglo-Maratha War.[1] The family traces their origin to 16th century India, when their ancestors came from present day Afghanistan to India during the period of the Lodi dynasty.[1].
Thought 2: The initial search for "Nawab of Pataudi" gives information about the state and its establishment, but not a list of the Nawabs or who held the title. I need to find the holders of the title. I will try to refine my search to "Nawab of Pataudi holders" or "list of Nawabs of Pataudi".
Action 2: Search[Nawabs of Pataudi]
Observation 2: Pataudi State was a small princely state in India, established in 1804 by the East India Company rule in India.. The state formed a part of the Delhi Territory in the Ceded and Conquered Provinces. It was under the suzerainty of the Commissioner of Delhi. It had an area of 52 square miles and included one town, Pataudi, and 40 villages, ruled by the Pataudi family.. The state of Pataudi was established in 1804 by the British East India Company, when Faiz Talab Khan, an Afghan Pashtun warlord of the Barech tribe, who was made the first Nawab, aided them in their battle against the Maratha Empire, during the Second Anglo-Maratha War.[1] The family traces their origin to 16th century India, when their ancestors came from present day Afghanistan to India during the period of the Lodi dynasty.[1].
Thought 3: The search for "Nawabs of Pataudi" returned the same general information about the state. I need to find a list of the Nawabs. I will try searching for "Nawab of Pataudi list" or "rulers of Pataudi".
Action 3: Search[Nawab of Pataudi list]

Thought 4: The search for "Nawab of Pataudi list" did not yield a direct list, but it did suggest "Iftikhar Ali Khan Pataudi" and "Saif Ali Khan (redirect from Sajid Ali Khan Pataudi)". These are likely individuals who held the title. I will search for "Pataudi family" to see if it provides a lineage or list of Nawabs.
Action 4: Search[Pataudi family]
Observation 4: The Pataudi family is an Indian show business family, primarily working in India's Hindi film industry, commonly known as 'Bollywood'.. They are also noted as the family of erstwhile nawabs of the former princely state of Pataudi, from which they take their name.[1] Faiz Talab Khan, an ethnic Pashtun from the Barech tribe of Kandahar, Afghanistan, became the first Nawab of Pataudi State in 1804,[2][1] after he aided the British East India Company in their battle against the Maratha Empire, during the Second Anglo-Maratha War.[2]. His descendants subsequently ruled the state until 1949, when it was merged with East Punjab and acceded to Dominion of India.[3] The Pataudis retained their titles and were granted privy purses until both were abolished by the Indian government in 1971.[4] Some of the family members migrated to the newly formed Muslim-majority Dominion of Pakistan, including Sher Ali Khan Pataudi, who served as a major-general in the Pakistan Army. The last ruling nawab was Iftikhar Ali Khan Pataudi and the last recognised titular nawab was his son Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi. The current patriarch of the family is Saif Ali Khan.[5].
